supporting_evidence.summary: significant deviations in scope [all services]: emailservice_latency-90 z=897.7 (4488.5%); shippingservice_latency-90 z=473.34 (2366.7%); checkoutservice_latency-90 z=356.38 (1781.9%); paymentservice_latency-50 z=229.91 (1149.6%)
traces for emailservice: SIGNIFICANT change; own spans self-time p50 0.2->0.2ms (1.03x), errors 0.0->0.0; inbound calls self-time p50 3.7->204.09ms (55.23x), errors 0.0->0.0

alternatives_rejected.why: Its latency-90 deviation (z=473) is about half of emailservice's (z=897.7) in E1, and it has no trace data to back a separate fault; most likely spillover in the shared checkout flow.

Its latency-90 deviation (z=356) is smaller than its callee emailservice's (E1); a slow caller would not inflate a callee's own latency metric. Its rise fits waiting on emailservice, whose inbound latency rose 55x (E2).
Its deviation (latency-50 z=229) is the smallest of the four in E1, consistent with secondary impact rather than the origin.

proposed_fix.description: Inspect and remove any injected network delay (for example tc/netem rules or a chaos experiment) on the emailservice pod or its network path. If none is found, restart or reschedule the emailservice pod, then confirm that checkoutservice's latency to emailservice returns to its baseline of about 4ms.
